function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live weather data. You can check a reliable weather service (e.g., the Weather Channel, AccuWeather, or a local Russian meteorological site) for the current temperature in Moscow.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What weather is now in Moscow, in Celsius?" They want current weather in Moscow in Celsius. We need to provide the answer. There's no tool for weather. We can respond with a placeholder or we can say we don't have real-time data. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. So we should say we cannot fetch real-time data. We can suggest using a weather API or checking a website. So we should respond that we can't provide real-time weather.
